mainTopic: The oaths of the four guardians, and when a guardian who falsely claims theft pays כפל or חומש.
overview: This amud opens at the end of רמי בר חמא's rule that all four guardians (שומרים) owe the oath of מודה במקצת only when they admit part of a claim and deny part. רבא then shows where the תורה teaches this for each guardian. Next, רבי חייא בר יוסף rules that a guardian who falsely claims a thief stole the deposit pays כפל only if he used the item for himself, and he learns this from 'אם לא שלח ידו'. In רבי יוחנן's name, רבי חייא בר אבא says the law applies even to an animal still standing at its trough. רבי זירא asks whether that means using the item cancels the כפל. A proof from a guardian who swore 'lost' and then 'stolen' is pushed aside, because the first oath already ended his duty to the owner. רב ששת then reads the same פסוק the opposite way: a guardian who used the item is exempt from כפל. He defends this against רב נחמן's argument from the three oaths. Finally, רמי בר חמא asks whether the money or the oath behind the כפל exempts the guardian from חומש, and the גמרא begins building a case to test it, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: All four guardians need a partial admission to owe an oath
steps.stepSummary: רמי בר חמא's statement ends: all four kinds of guardians only owe an oath if they admit part of the claim and deny part.
steps.simpleTranslation: [The four guardians] need a denial of part and an admission of part. They are: an unpaid guardian, a borrower, a paid guardian, and a renter.
steps.whatsHappening: We are hearing the end of רמי בר חמא's rule. Every type of guardian owes an oath only when he admits part of the claim and denies the rest.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally the oath of מודה במקצת is taught for a loan. רמי בר חמא says it also applies to all four guardians: שומר חנם, שואל, שומר שכר, and שוכר. If the guardian denies everything, or admits everything, this oath does not apply.

keyTerms.meaning: A paid guardian (same as שׁוֹמֵר שָׂכָר)

steps.confusionAlert: This is not the usual guardian's oath that he was not negligent. This is the oath of מודה במקצת, which comes up when the guardian admits only part of what the owner claims he received.

phrases.english: require denial of part
phrases.notes: This finishes a sentence that started earlier: 'The four guardians require...'

phrases.english: and admission of part,
and these are they:
an unpaid guardian and a borrower,
a paid guardian and a renter.

steps.mimraCoreRuling: All four שומרים owe a שבועה only when they partly admit and partly deny the claim.

steps.title: רבא asks for the source of רמי בר חמא's rule
steps.stepSummary: רבא asks what the reason is behind רמי בר חמא's rule.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: What is the reason of רמי בר חמא?
steps.whatsHappening: רבא asks where רמי בר חמא gets his rule for all four guardians. This sets up the next steps, where רבא answers for each guardian one at a time.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Saying that all four guardians need מודה במקצת is a claim that needs a source. רבא will find a source in the פסוקים for each one.

phrases.english: Rava said:
What is the reason of Rami bar Chama?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source of the rule in step 1.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source in the פסוקים for applying מודה במקצת to each of the four guardians.

steps.title: Sources for the unpaid and the paid guardian
steps.stepSummary: For the שומר חנם the פסוק says 'כי הוא זה' outright. The שומר שכר learns it from the שומר חנם through a גזירה שוה on the word 'giving'.
steps.simpleTranslation: For an unpaid guardian, it is written clearly about him: 'that this is it.' A paid guardian learns 'giving' and 'giving' from the unpaid guardian.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives the first two sources. The unpaid guardian has a clear פסוק, and the paid guardian is linked to him by a matching word.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'כי הוא זה' ('this is it') are in the section about the שומר חנם, and they are the source for partial admission. The sections for both the שומר חנם and the שומר שכר open with 'כי יתן איש' ('if a man gives'). That shared word lets the rule carry over by גזירה שוה.

keyTerms.meaning: 'That this is it', the words that point to a partial admission
'Giving', the shared word used for the גזירה שוה

phrases.english: An unpaid guardian: it is clearly written about him:
"that this is it."
A paid guardian: he learns
"giving"–"giving" from the unpaid guardian.
phrases.notes: Both sections start with 'if a man gives to his neighbor' (שמות 22:6 and 22:9), so that shared word links them.

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: שומר חנם: a clear פסוק. שומר שכר: a גזירה שוה from the word 'giving'.

steps.title: Source for the borrower
steps.stepSummary: The borrower is included because the extra 'ו' in 'וכי ישאל' links his section to the one before it.
steps.simpleTranslation: A borrower: 'And if a man borrows.' The letter ו adds to the earlier topic.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives the source for the borrower. The word 'and' at the start of the borrower's פסוק connects him to the guardian section that comes right before.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is a rule that a 'ו' (and) joins a passage to the passage before it. So the borrower takes on the laws of the guardian section that comes before, including מודה במקצת.

keyTerms.meaning: The letter ו adds on to the earlier topic

phrases.english: A borrower: "And if a man borrows,"
the vav adds to the first topic.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the list of sources with the third guardian.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The 'ו' of 'וכי ישאל' connects the borrower to the guardian section before it.

steps.title: The renter needs no source of his own
steps.stepSummary: The renter is treated either like a paid guardian or like an unpaid one, depending on the opinion. Either way he is already covered.
steps.simpleTranslation: A renter: according to the one who says he is like a paid guardian, he is the same as a paid guardian. According to the one who says he is like an unpaid guardian, he is the same as an unpaid guardian.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא explains that the renter does not need his own source. He simply follows whichever guardian he is compared to.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is a disagreement over whether a שוכר has the laws of a שומר שכר or of a שומר חנם. Both of those were already shown to need מודה במקצת, so under either opinion the renter needs it too.

keyTerms.meaning: According to the one who says

steps.whatToRemember: Each of the four guardians gets the מודה במקצת rule: שומר חנם from a clear פסוק, שומר שכר from a גזירה שוה, שואל from the extra 'ו', and שוכר by following whichever guardian he is compared to.

phrases.aramaic: שׂוֹכֵר – אִי לְמַאן דְּאָמַר כְּשׁוֹמֵר שָׂכָר,
phrases.english: A renter: if according to the one who says he is like a paid guardian,
he is the same as a paid guardian;
if according to the one who says he is like an unpaid guardian,
he is the same as an unpaid guardian.

steps.triggerLanguage: שׂוֹכֵר אִי לְמַאן דְּאָמַר כְּשׁוֹמֵר שָׂכָר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes רבא's answer with the fourth guardian.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The שוכר follows either the שומר שכר or the שומר חנם, and both are already covered.

steps.title: A false theft claim brings liability only after the guardian used the item
steps.stepSummary: רבי חייא בר יוסף rules that a guardian who falsely claims a deposit was stolen is not liable until he has used the item for himself.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי חייא בר יוסף said: One who claims a thief took a deposit is not liable until he puts his hand on it.
steps.whatsHappening: A new teaching starts here. A guardian who lies that a thief stole the deposit is only liable once he has used the item for himself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The case is a guardian who falsely claims 'it was stolen' (טענת גנב). רבי חייא בר יוסף adds a condition: the liability only applies if he did שליחות יד, meaning he used the item for his own needs.

keyTerms.meaning: A deposit left with a guardian
That he 'sends his hand' into it, meaning he uses it for himself (שליחות יד)

phrases.english: And Rabbi Chiyya bar Yosef said:
One who makes the claim of a thief regarding a deposit,
phrases.notes: He means a guardian who falsely says 'a thief stole it.'

phrases.aramaic: אֵינוֹ חַיָּיב עַד שֶׁיִּשְׁלַח בּוֹ יָד.
phrases.english: is not liable until he puts his hand on it.
phrases.notes: 'Liable' here means the double payment that goes with a false theft claim.

steps.mimraCoreRuling: Liability for a false טענת גנב applies only once the guardian has done שליחות יד.

steps.title: What is the reason for this rule?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the source of רבי חייא בר יוסף's rule.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why the guardian must have used the item to be liable. This sets up the פסוק that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Adding a condition like this to the law needs support. The answer will come from a close reading of the פסוק.

phrases.english: What is the reason?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source of step 6.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why liability depends on שליחות יד.

steps.title: The verse shows the case is about one who used the item
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק says the guardian goes to court to check 'if he did not put his hand' on the item. So if he did, he is liable, and the case must be one where he used it.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'And the owner of the house shall come near to the judges, if he did not put his hand on his neighbor's goods.' This implies that if he did put his hand on it, he is liable. That is to say, we are dealing with a case where he put his hand on it.
steps.whatsHappening: The proof comes from the wording of the פסוק. It shows that the liability is tied to the guardian having used the item.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק makes the court's question 'did he put his hand on it?' From that we learn that putting his hand on it is what makes him liable. So the whole section, including the double payment, is talking about a guardian who used the item.

keyTerms.meaning: Literally 'the owner of the house'; here it means the guardian

steps.whatToRemember: According to רבי חייא בר יוסף, a guardian who lies that a thief stole the deposit is liable only once he has used it for himself. He learns this from 'אם לא שלח ידו'. Others disagree later on the amud (steps 9 and 14).

phrases.english: "And the owner of the house shall come near to the judges,

phrases.aramaic: אִם לֹא שָׁלַח יָדוֹ בִּמְלֶאכֶת רֵעֵהוּ״,
phrases.english: if he did not put his hand on his neighbor's goods,"

phrases.aramaic: מִכְּלָל דְּאִי שָׁלַח בָּהּ יָד – מִיחַיַּיב;
phrases.english: this implies that if he put his hand on it, he is liable;
that is to say, we are dealing with where he put his hand on it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 7 with a פסוק.
steps.raayaObject: רבי חייא בר יוסף's rule that liability needs שליחות יד.
steps.raayaSupportSource: שמות 22:7, 'אם לא שלח ידו במלאכת רעהו', read by inference.

steps.title: The double payment law applies to an animal still at its trough
steps.stepSummary: רבי חייא בר אבא reports that רבי יוחנן said the law of כפל for a false theft claim was taught about an animal still standing at its trough.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חייא בר אבא said: רבי יוחנן said the law was taught about an animal that is still standing at its feeding trough.
steps.whatsHappening: A new statement comes in. In the name of רבי יוחנן, רבי חייא בר אבא says the guardian pays כפל even when the animal is just standing at its trough and he never used it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An animal 'standing at its trough' means the guardian is still watching it for the owner and has not taken it for himself. That is the opposite of רבי חייא בר יוסף's view in step 6, where the guardian is liable only after using the item.

keyTerms.meaning: Standing at its feeding trough, meaning the animal is untouched and the guardian has not used it
They taught; this refers to a ruling learned in a earlier source

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up a direct contrast with רבי חייא בר יוסף and opens the question of what happens when the guardian did use the item.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לְהוּ רַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר אַבָּא,
phrases.english: Rabbi Chiyya bar Abba said to them,
this is what Rabbi Yochanan said:
They taught it about an animal standing at its trough.
phrases.notes: 'It' is the rule that a guardian who falsely claims theft pays double.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a different view from רבי חייא בר יוסף: using the item is not required for liability.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The law of כפל for a false theft claim applies even when the guardian never used the animal.

steps.title: Only an unused animal, or also a used one?
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא asks whether רבי יוחנן meant only an unused animal, because using it makes it the guardian's, or whether he meant even an unused one in addition to a used one.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי זירא asked: Did he mean only an animal at its trough, because if the guardian used it he already acquired it and the oath does nothing? Or did he mean even an animal at its trough, and certainly one he used?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי זירא asks what exactly רבי יוחנן meant by 'standing at its trough.' The rest of the passage tries to answer him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Option one: once the guardian uses the item, it already belongs to him as stolen property, so a later false oath changes nothing and there is no כפל. Option two: כפל applies to both cases, and the unused case was mentioned because it is the bigger חידוש.

keyTerms.meaning: He 'put his hand' on it, meaning he used the item for himself
He acquired it; it now counts as his, stolen, and he carries full responsibility for it

steps.confusionAlert: 'Even standing at its trough' does not mean 'only standing.' It means the unused case is included too, on top of the used case.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַבִּי זֵירָא לְרַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר אַבָּא:
phrases.english: Rabbi Zeira said to Rabbi Chiyya bar Abba:
Is he saying it only about one standing at its trough,
but if he used it, he acquired it,
and an oath does nothing for it at all;
phrases.notes: Since it is already his, a later false oath cannot make him pay double.

phrases.aramaic: אוֹ דִלְמָא, אֲפִילּוּ עוֹמֶדֶת עַל אֲבוּסָהּ קָאָמַר?
phrases.english: or perhaps he is saying even one standing at its trough?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks how far רבי יוחנן's ruling in step 9 reaches.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does using the item cancel the כפל from a later false oath, or does כפל apply in both the used and unused cases?

steps.title: A similar ruling: two false oaths, and the guardian is exempt
steps.stepSummary: רבי חייא בר אבא did not hear an answer, but he brings רבי יוחנן's ruling that a guardian who swore 'lost' and then swore 'stolen' does not pay כפל. He suggests the reason is that the first oath already made the item his.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said: I didn't hear this, but I heard something like it. רבי אסי said in the name of רבי יוחנן: if a guardian claimed 'it was lost' and swore, then claimed 'a thief took it' and swore, and witnesses came, he is exempt. Isn't the reason that he acquired the item with the first oath?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי חייא בר אבא admits he has no direct answer. He brings a similar case to try to show that once the guardian has taken the item for himself, a later false oath does not lead to כפל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In this case the guardian's second oath, the false theft claim, would normally bring כפל, yet he is exempt. If the reason is that the first false oath made the item his, then using the item should do the same. That would mean 'standing at its trough' is only the unused case.

keyTerms.meaning: A claim that the item was lost
A claim that a thief took it; this is the claim that brings כפל

phrases.english: He said to him: This I did not hear,
but something like it I did hear;

phrases.aramaic: דְּאָמַר רַבִּי אַסִּי אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: as Rabbi Asi said in the name of Rabbi Yochanan:
one who claims 'it was lost' and swears,
and then claims 'a thief took it' and swears,
and witnesses came — he is exempt.
phrases.notes: The witnesses show both claims were lies. He is exempt from paying double for the second claim.

phrases.english: What is the reason?
Is it not because he acquired it with the first oath?

steps.triggerLanguage: זוֹ לֹא שָׁמַעְתִּי, כַּיּוֹצֵא בָּהּ שָׁמַעְתִּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tries to answer רבי זירא's question using a similar ruling of רבי יוחנן.
steps.raayaObject: That once a guardian has taken the item for himself, a later false oath does not lead to כפל, so רבי יוחנן's ruling covers only the unused animal.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי אסי quoting רבי יוחנן: a guardian who swore 'lost' and then 'stolen' is exempt from כפל.

steps.title: No proof: the first oath ended his duty to the owner
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא rejects the proof. The guardian is exempt because the first oath already finished his duty to the owner, not because he acquired the item.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: No. He is exempt because the first oath already took him out of the owner's hands.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי זירא pushes back on the proof. He gives a different reason for the exemption in רבי אסי's case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once the guardian swore the first time, he had done what he owed the owner, so the second oath does not count toward כפל. This reason has nothing to do with acquiring the item. So the case says nothing about whether using the item cancels כפל.

keyTerms.meaning: He is done with the owner; his duty to the owner has already been met

phrases.english: He said to him: No,

phrases.aramaic: הוֹאִיל וְיָצָא יְדֵי בְּעָלִים בִּשְׁבוּעָה רִאשׁוֹנָה.
phrases.english: since he already left the owner's hands with the first oath.
phrases.notes: The first oath settled things with the owner, so there is nothing left for the second oath to work on.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: לָא, הוֹאִיל וְיָצָא יְדֵי בְּעָלִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the reason proposed in step 11 for רבי יוחנן's ruling.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the proof completely; רבי זירא's question stays open.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The exemption can be explained by the first oath ending the duty to the owner, without any idea of acquiring the item.

steps.title: Another report of רבי יוחנן confirms רבי זירא's reason
steps.stepSummary: A second chain of transmission quotes רבי יוחנן giving the same ruling, and it states רבי זירא's reason outright: the first oath ended the guardian's duty to the owner.
steps.simpleTranslation: This was also said: רבי אבין said in the name of רבי אילעא, in the name of רבי יוחנן: a guardian who claimed a deposit was lost and swore, then claimed it was stolen and swore, and witnesses came, is exempt, since the first oath already took him out of the owner's hands.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings another report of רבי יוחנן's words to back up רבי זירא. This report states the reason that רבי זירא gave.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here רבי יוחנן himself says 'since he left the owner's hands with the first oath.' That confirms the exemption is not about acquiring the item. So רבי חייא בר אבא's proof does not work.

keyTerms.meaning: It was also stated; this brings a supporting teaching
A deposit left with a guardian

steps.whatToRemember: A guardian who swore falsely that an item was lost and then swore falsely that it was stolen does not pay כפל. The reason is that the first oath already ended his duty to the owner, not that he acquired the item. רבי זירא's question about a guardian who used the item is left without a proof.

phrases.english: It was also stated:

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי אָבִין אָמַר רַבִּי אִילְעָא אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: Rabbi Avin said in the name of Rabbi Ila, in the name of Rabbi Yochanan:
one who claims a deposit was lost and swears,
and then claims it was stolen and swears,
and witnesses came — he is exempt,

phrases.aramaic: הוֹאִיל וְיָצָא יְדֵי בְּעָלִים בִּשְׁבוּעָה רִאשׁוֹנָה.
phrases.english: since he already left the owner's hands with the first oath.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports רבי זירא's rejection in step 12 with a direct quote of רבי יוחנן.
steps.raayaObject: רבי זירא's reason for the exemption: the first oath ended the guardian's duty to the owner.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי אבין quoting רבי אילעא quoting רבי יוחנן.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The exemption in the two-oath case rests on the first oath ending the duty to the owner, not on acquiring the item.

steps.title: A guardian who already used the deposit is exempt from double payment
steps.stepSummary: רב ששת rules that a guardian who used the deposit for himself and then falsely claimed it was stolen is exempt from כפל, learning this from the words 'אם לא שלח ידו' in the פסוק.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ששת said: If a guardian claims a thief stole the deposit, but he had already used it for himself, he is exempt from paying double. Why? The תורה says the owner of the house comes to the judges 'if he has not put forth his hand.' So if he did put forth his hand, he is exempt.
steps.whatsHappening: רב ששת gives a new ruling. A guardian who used the deposit for himself does not pay כפל, even if his 'thief' claim turns out to be false.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק about כפל for a false 'thief' claim describes a guardian who did not use the item. רב ששת reads that as a limit: the כפל law covers only that case. Once the guardian has used the item, the כפל law does not apply to him.

keyTerms.meaning: The claim that a thief stole the item
A deposit, something left with a guardian to watch
He used it for himself (literally, 'put his hand on it')
The Merciful One, meaning the תורה

steps.whyThisMatters: רב ששת reads the same words that רבי חייא בר יוסף read in step 8, 'אם לא שלח ידו', and reaches the opposite result. For רבי חייא בר יוסף, using the item is what brings כפל. For רב ששת, using the item removes כפל. His view also matches the first side of רבי זירא's question in step 10.

phrases.english: Rav Sheshet said:
One who claims 'a thief took it' about a deposit,
once he has used it for himself, he is exempt.
phrases.notes: He means exempt from כפל, the double payment.

phrases.english: What is the reason?
This is what the Torah is saying:
"And the owner of the house shall come near to the judges,
if he has not put forth his hand, etc."
This implies that if he did put forth his hand, he is exempt.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב שֵׁשֶׁת: הַטּוֹעֵן טַעֲנַת גַּנָּב בְּפִקָּדוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees directly with רבי חייא בר יוסף (steps 6–8). He reads the same פסוק, 'אם לא שלח ידו', the opposite way: using the item exempts the guardian from כפל instead of being what makes him liable.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A guardian who used the deposit and then falsely claimed theft is exempt from כפל, based on 'אם לא שלח ידו'.

steps.title: The three oaths seem to show that using the deposit still brings double payment
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן challenges רב ששת. Among the three oaths a guardian swears, 'I did not use it' sits next to 'it is not in my possession,' and that oath brings כפל when it turns out false. So a false 'I did not use it' oath should also bring כפל.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן said to him: But the court makes the guardian swear three oaths: I was not careless with it; I did not use it for myself; it is not in my possession. Isn't the 'I did not use it' oath like the 'not in my possession' oath? If it turns out the item is in his possession, he is liable. So too, if it turns out he used it, he should be liable!
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן attacks רב ששת's ruling. He compares the oath 'I did not use it' to the oath 'it is not in my possession.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: A false 'it is not in my possession' oath makes the guardian pay כפל. רב נחמן argues that the 'I did not use it' oath belongs to the same group, so it should work the same way. That would mean a guardian who used the item does pay כפל, which is the opposite of רב ששת's ruling.

keyTerms.meaning: The matter comes out, it becomes known

phrases.english: Rav Nachman said to him:
But don't they make him swear three oaths:
"An oath that I was not careless with it";
"An oath that I did not use it for myself";
"An oath that it is not in my possession."
What, is it not so that
"the oath that I did not use it"
is like "the oath that it is not in my possession"?
Just as with "the oath that it is not in my possession,"

phrases.aramaic: כִּי מִיגַּלְּיָא מִילְּתָא דְּאִיתֵיהּ בִּרְשׁוּתֵיהּ – חַיָּיב;
phrases.english: when it comes out that it is in his possession, he is liable;
phrases.notes: Liable here means he pays כפל.

phrases.english: so too with "the oath that I did not use it,"

phrases.aramaic: כִּי מִיגַּלְּיָא מִילְּתָא דִּשְׁלַח בָּהּ יָד – חַיָּיב!
phrases.english: when it comes out that he used it, he should be liable!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב נַחְמָן, וַהֲלֹא שָׁלֹשׁ שָׁבוּעוֹת מַשְׁבִּיעִין אוֹתוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב ששת's ruling from step 14.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב ששת's ruling that a guardian who used the deposit is exempt from כפל.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The 'I did not use it' oath is grouped with the 'not in my possession' oath, which brings כפל when false. So a false 'I did not use it' oath should bring כפל too.

steps.title: The 'I did not use it' oath can be compared to the 'I was not careless' oath instead
steps.stepSummary: רב ששת answers that the 'I did not use it' oath can just as well be compared to the 'I was not careless' oath, which brings no כפל when it turns out false. So the three oaths prove nothing.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ששת said to him: No. The 'I did not use it' oath is like the 'I was not careless' oath. If it turns out he was careless, he is exempt from double payment. So too, if it turns out he used it, he is exempt from double payment.
steps.whatsHappening: רב ששת defends his ruling. He pairs the 'I did not use it' oath with a different oath on the list.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A false 'I was not careless' oath does not bring כפל, so comparing to it gives the opposite result from רב נחמן's comparison. Since the oath can be matched with either neighbor, the list of three oaths gives no proof. רב ששת's ruling, which rests on the פסוק, stands.

keyTerms.meaning: No, that is not a proof
Double payment, paid by a thief or by a guardian whose 'thief' claim was false

steps.whatToRemember: רב ששת's ruling survives: a guardian who used the deposit is exempt from כפל. The comparison between the oaths works in both directions, so it decides nothing.

phrases.english: He said to him: No;
"the oath that I did not use it"
is like "that I was not careless with it."
Just as with "the oath that I was not careless with it,"

phrases.aramaic: כִּי מִיגַּלְּיָא מִילְּתָא דְּפָשַׁע בָּהּ, פָּטוּר מִכֶּפֶל;
phrases.english: when it comes out that he was careless with it, he is exempt from double payment;
so too with "the oath that I did not use it,"

phrases.aramaic: כִּי מִיגַּלְּיָא מִילְּתָא דִּשְׁלַח בָּהּ יָד, פָּטוּר מִכֶּפֶל.
phrases.english: when it comes out that he used it, he is exempt from double payment.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: לָא; שְׁבוּעָה שֶׁלֹּא שָׁלַחְתִּי בָּהּ יָד דּוּמְיָא דְּשֶׁלֹּא פָּשַׁעְתִּי בָּהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב נחמן's challenge from step 15.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Offers a different comparison that cancels out the challenger's comparison.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The 'I did not use it' oath works like the 'not in my possession' oath, so a false one brings כפל.
steps.terutzMaskana: It can equally work like the 'I was not careless' oath, which brings no כפל. So the list proves nothing, and the ruling from the פסוק stands.

steps.title: Is it the money or the oath that cancels the one-fifth payment?
steps.stepSummary: רמי בר חמא asks why a guardian who owes כפל is exempt from חומש. Is it the money owed as כפל that exempts him, or the oath that made him owe כפל?
steps.simpleTranslation: רמי בר חמא asked: Is it the money that makes him owe double payment that exempts him from the extra fifth? Or perhaps it is the oath that makes him owe double payment that exempts him from the extra fifth?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new question. רמי בר חמא wants to know exactly what causes the guardian's exemption from חומש.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A guardian who owes כפל does not also pay חומש. רמי בר חמא asks what creates that exemption. One option is the money itself: since he pays כפל, he does not pay a fifth. The other option is the oath: the same oath that brought כפל cancels the fifth.

keyTerms.meaning: The extra fifth added by one who swore falsely about money

phrases.english: Rami bar Chama asked:
Is it the money that makes him owe double payment
phrases.notes: Someone who swears falsely to keep money normally adds a fifth; a guardian who pays כפל does not.

phrases.english: that exempts him from the fifth,
or perhaps it is the oath that makes him owe double payment
that exempts him from the fifth?

steps.triggerLanguage: בָּעֵי רָמֵי בַּר חָמָא: מָמוֹן הַמְחַיְּיבוֹ כֶּפֶל פּוֹטְרוֹ מִן הַחוֹמֶשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic about how כפל and חומש relate to each other.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the exemption from חומש comes from the money owed as כפל or from the oath that caused the כפל.

steps.title: Building a case where the two possibilities differ
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks in what situation רמי בר חמא's question would actually matter. It starts describing a guardian who swore two different false oaths: first that the deposit was stolen, then that it was lost.
steps.simpleTranslation: What would the case look like? For example, the guardian claimed a thief took the deposit and swore to it. Then he went back, claimed it was lost, and swore to that.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up the next move. Before answering רמי בר חמא, it first builds a case where 'the money exempts him' and 'the oath exempts him' would lead to different results.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Usually the כפל money and the oath that caused it come together, so you cannot tell which one exempts him from חומש. Here the guardian swears twice about the same deposit, once with a טענת גנב and once with a טענת אבד. That pulls the two factors apart so the question can be tested. The case is not finished yet, and the גמרא keeps describing it on the next amud.

keyTerms.meaning: What are the circumstances? A request to picture the exact case
A claim that a thief stole the deposit
A claim that the deposit was lost
And he went back, changing his story

steps.confusionAlert: Both of these claims are false. The guardian is not telling two true stories. He is lying twice, under oath each time, in two different ways.

phrases.english: What are the circumstances?
phrases.notes: He means: in what case would it make a difference whether the money or the oath is what exempts him from חומש?

phrases.english: For example, where he claimed that a thief stole it and swore to that,
and then he went back, claimed that it was lost, and swore to that;

steps.triggerLanguage: הֵיכִי דָּמֵי? כְּגוֹן שֶׁטָּעַן טַעֲנַת גַּנָּב וְנִשְׁבַּע
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts defining the concrete case where רמי בר חמא's two possibilities from step 17 would lead to different rulings.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: In what real case would it matter whether the כפל money or the oath behind it is what exempts the guardian from חומש?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The answer begins here and is still incomplete: a guardian who swore falsely with a טענת גנב, then swore falsely again with a טענת אבד.
